text:
alex_support: heads up — SilverStream opened a support ticket: sudden throughput drop and p99 latency spike started ~09:15 UTC for their production endpoint. they attached a short trace and said no config changes on their side.

maria_runtime: thanks. can you paste the ticket link + sample request IDs? any change in model variant?

alex_support: ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SS-1245 sample req ids: r_8a3f2, r_8a7c9, r_8b1d0 they said model pinned to gpt-small-v1. no rollout logs on their side. :thinking_face:

jon_sre: I see a scaling event around 09:12 UTC for that pool in infra logs — autoscaler bounced a node due to OOM and then added capacity. could cause queuing. pulling k8s events now.

maria_runtime: good lead. if autoscaler bounced, requests might have been routed to a different node with cold KV cache. that explains p99. can someone run a quick qps replay/bench against their shard to reproduce? use low token lengths matching their trace.

sarah_bench: running lightweight repro now: `rctl bench --target=customer:silverstream --duration=3m --concurrency=8 --tokens=150` will post results.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.15-3f9a applied to runtime-pool-a at 08:58 UTC

maria_runtime: @jon_sre can you confirm whether the OOM was due to a leak or a spike? also paste the kernel selector logs for that node.

jon_sre: OOM stack points to memory pressure in the quantized allocator on node ip-10-4-2-11. allocator logs: `ERR: quant_alloc: exceeded soft limit 4.0GB` — looks like a spike in concurrent KV snapshots. linking logs: /logs/alloc/10-4-2-11/2026-03-15-09.json

kevin_custsuccess: pinged SilverStream PM — they confirm some batched jobs kicked off at ~09:10 (internal data sync) which would increase concurrency. they can stagger.

alex_support: adding that to the ticket. customer asked if we can do a temporary mitigation — maybe route them to a smaller batch size or fallback model.

maria_runtime: for quick mitigation: 1) throttle their max_concurrency at the edge to 6, 2) enable fallback to gpt-tiny-v1 for requests > 200 tokens, 3) pin routes to dedicated capacity with burst disabled until we stabilize. I'll open a canary with rate-limits.

sarah_bench: bench results (after 2m): concurrency=8 produced p50=120ms p95=860ms p99=2.3s throughput=45r/s. repro with concurrency=6: p50=110ms p95=420ms p99=780ms throughput=34r/s. looks consistent with queuing.

maria_runtime: thanks Sarah. can we run a flamegraph/profile from the affected node for the window 09:10–09:20? Use `profiler snapshot --node ip-10-4-2-11 --since 09:10 --until 09:20 --format=flame`.

jon_sre: grabbing profile now. noticed a GC bump from the allocator and repeated KV cache population. might be a cache eviction storm due to increased context variety from their batched jobs.

maria_runtime: interesting — if batch jobs introduce many unique prefixes, prefix/KV cache gets churn and causes higher memory + miss rate. mitigation: increase KV cache size on that pool temporarily and enable prefix coalescing. I'll create a runtime change request.

deploy-bot: config change request CR-998 queued for runtime-pool-a: "kv_cache.size += 25% for pool-a" — requires approval.

kevin_custsuccess: SilverStream OK to stagger their internal jobs by 2 minutes and accept temporary throttling. they want ETA for fix.

maria_runtime: action items: 1) jon to approve and apply KV cache bump on pool-a (temporary) 2) sarah to run a follow-up bench after change 3) alex to update ticket with mitigation steps and ask customer to stagger jobs 4) i'll add a follow-up to analytics to detect bursty prefix churn. owner: maria_runtime. target: 30m.

jon_sre: approving CR-998 now. applying KV cache bump. will monitor memory and OOM alarms.

sarah_bench: re-run queued: `rctl bench --target=customer:silverstream --duration=3m --concurrency=8 --tokens=150` — initial results after KV bump: p99 down to 950ms, throughput up to 52r/s. still slightly elevated but much better.

maria_runtime: great. i'll keep the canary rate-limit in place for one hour and then remove if stable. alex please confirm ticket update and close if customer satisfied.

alex_support: updated ticket with actions and results. customer reports tail latency improved and will monitor. they accepted the stagger plan. closing once we remove temporary throttles. :white_check_mark:

maria_runtime: follow-up: add alerting rule to detect sudden prefix entropy increases per-customer. will post PR today to monitoring repo.

jon_sre: will keep an eye on node memory; if OOM recurs we'll investigate allocator tuning.

sarah_bench: leaving the bench run in CI to periodically replay for 2h to ensure stability.

kevin_custsuccess: thanks everyone — good cross-team coordination.

maria_runtime: thanks all. summarizing in a short postmortem if this reoccurs.

alex_support: marking this thread resolved in Slack.
